  Seasonal Assessment: Weather

Adam Simkowski and Ella Dankanics, MISO Meteorologists
 Last winter featured a weaker La Niña, but we still saw periods of significant cold

• Last winter is not considered an analog for this upcoming winter.
• Near- to/below-normal temperatures occurred across much of
 MISO, particularly the North and Central Regions.

• MISO experienced 7 days with systemwide temperatures ≤10°F,
 including 5 days during Winter Storm Fern.

• Similar to Winter Storm Enzo the year prior, Winter Storm Fern
 demonstrated that significant winter impacts can still occur
 despite the overall seasonal pattern.

• Below-normal precipitation was prevalent across much of the
 Central and South Regions.

• Given the weak La Niña, short-duration cold extremes were still
 a significant feature of the winter.

                                                                                4
 Stronger El Niño winters usually produce above normal temperatures in MISO’s North
and Central Regions
                                                                                               What is El Niño?
                                                                                                                         • El Niño is the warm phase of ENSO, characterized by
                                                                                                                             warmer-than-normal ocean temperatures across the
                                                                                                                             central/eastern equatorial Pacific.

                                                                                                                         • Trade winds weaken, allowing warm surface water
                                                                                                                             that is normally concentrated in the western Pacific to
                                                                                                                             shift eastward.

                                                                                                                         • This shift changes tropical convection and
                                                                                                                             atmospheric circulation, which can alter the jet
                                                                                                                             stream and weather patterns across North America.

                                                                                                                         • El Niño typically develops during summer/fall, peaks
                                                                                                                             during winter, and weakens the following spring.




The El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is a recurring climate pattern involving changes in the temperature of waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean.   5

                                Adam and Ella’s Opinion

• The El Niño (ocean-atmosphere signal) is expected to be strong this winter, driving the
 underlying warmer pattern. Cold air outbreaks have a lower likelihood.
• Monitoring other atmospheric and oceanic signals will be less impactful to the MISO footprint
 this winter, rather we will continue to watch for the possibility of an El Niño weakening-
 especially closer to Feb.
• The polar vortex is expected to be more stable this winter, lowering the likelihood of
 prolonged arctic air outbreaks.
• A normal winter in the South Region is expected driven by cooler daytime high temperatures
 rather than colder minimum temperatures.
• Precipitation is expected to be elevated in MISO’s South Region due to a strong subtropical jet
 stream. We will monitor the possibility for increased icing across MISO South and Central
 Regions.


                                                                                        17
                                        Summary

• N/C Region expected to be warmer this winter.
• N/C Region temperatures could be impacted if the polar vortex becomes disrupted,
 allowing arctic air to push further south, but probability for this occurring is lower.
• Normal temperatures are expected in the South Region on average
• A drier pattern is expected with normal-to below-normal precipitation across the
 Great Lakes.
• Wetter conditions expected across much of the South Region throughout the winter.

 Matt Campbell, MISO Manager Operations Risk Assessment
 All-Hour and Dynamic Reserve Products to Manage Uncertainty



• MISO recently moved ramp and reserve regulation reserve products into production to
  manage uncertainty and give more visibility into challenging conditions across all operating
  hours.

• Under the multi-year uncertainty management initiative, MISO revamps methodology to
  quantify uncertainty and implements dynamic reserve process.

• This endeavor is a progress towards MISO's commitment to quantified, data-driven decisions
  to enhance uncertainty management.

                                               38
 All-Hour and Dynamic Reserve Products to Manage Uncertainty


• Dynamic Reg and Ramp products and all-hours uncertainty model recommendations position MISO to
   manage uncertainty and drive unit commitment decisions with higher confidence especially during
   more challenging system conditions.

• With better visibility into each hour of the operating day, MISO expects that there could be an
   increase in capacity advisories or higher reserves to manage those challenging hours to ensure we are
   able to meet our commitment thresholds.

• All- hour process not only identifies peak and 'worst hour' but provides uncertainty recommendations
   and insight into all hours.

• When commitment thresholds cannot be met or high-uncertainty exists, regulation requirements
   change along with additional STRs.




                                                                                             39
 Risk, Lessons and Experiences to Manage Uncertainty


Over the last 12 months, the winter and summer seasons of 2026 has provided MISO with
learning opportunities to improve forecasting accuracy, enhance the net-uncertainty model,
and leverage the dynamic ramp and reserve product in our seasonal outlook.
• Framing the right amount of risk and uncertainty on emergency ranges – what is the reality on the
   challenging hours and how best can 12GW LMRs be utilized. When LMRs have been requested,
   historically 6-7GW responded, with 1-3GW typically being self-scheduled

• Anticipating response when calling on AMEs
• NSI Uncertainty

 Why make an Emergency Declaration?

Emergency declarations enable the use of emergency-specific operational actions,
including:
• Emergency redispatch of generation (such as nuclear units)
• Starting emergency-only resources (e.g., AME units)
• Utilizing emergency operating ranges and limits
• Deploying demand response tools (EDRs and LMRs)
• Implementing Load Shedding
• Communicate externally



                                                                         77
 Transmission Warning
 Transmission Warning

A Transmission Warning should be declared when all of the following conditions are
met:
• There is 100MW or more of load at risk
• Normal congestion management tools have been exhausted and are not sufficient to
 mitigate risk
• Available emergency actions are not expected to be sufficient to mitigate risk (e.g.
 emergency ranges of units, emergency only units, LMRs, etc.)
• Facilities > 100kV have post-contingent flow greater than or equal to 115% of the
 highest emergency limit
• The RC determines that system conditions warrant heightened awareness of potential
 transmission system risk
                                                                                79
 IROL Emergency
 MISO’s IROL Definition Remains the Same

Cascading event with expected load loss of 1000 MW or more of load

• IROLs will be determined in the Expansion Planning and Operations Planning Horizon,
 and operating plans will be developed with TOPs as needed
• MISO’s Expansion Planning team will complete IROL analysis using planning criteria
• MISO’s Operations Planning team (FRES) will complete IROL analysis to determine if
 there are additional IROLs not defined by Expansion Planning based upon forecasted
 conditions for an operating day




                                                                            81
 IROL Emergency

An IROL Emergency happens when…

• A new real-time declaration indicating that a pre-defined IROL limit has been
 exceeded.
• The Reliability Coordinator declares an IROL Emergency when a predefined IROL is
  exceeded.
• Must be resolved in less than 30 minutes or Tv




                                                                              82
 Potential Cascading Emergency (PCE)
 In real-time, Reliability Coordinators will complete cascade analysis and
develop operating plans
• Potential cascading event if 5 lines trip and >= 300 MW load loss
  • The 300 MW load loss matches the DOE-417 reporting requirements
• Cascade analysis will occur when post-contingent flow is >= 115% of the emergency rating (aligns with
 PRC-023)
  • If the cascade event criteria is met, then
      • MISO RC will request from TOP the highest rating prior to load shed, which may include the relay
        trip setting
      • Develop pre-contingent action plan, including load shed plan. Actions based on the highest
        ratings before load shed are to be clear and executable
• If the cascade event criteria is not met, then:
  • Continue cascade analysis when post-contingent flows are >=125% of the Emergency Rating


                                                                                            84
 Potential Cascading Emergency

A Potential Cascading Emergency is…
• When a cascade analysis identifies a scenario where 5 lines trip and >= 300 MW load loss.
• Cascade analysis will occur when post-contingent flow is >= 115% of the Emergency Rating.
• When unsolved contingencies or stability limit exceedances indicate an unknown operating state with
   a potential loss of 300 MW, per RC discretion.

• Any operating condition where it is reasonable for the RC to expect that conditions will worsen and
   will potentially meet the criteria of a PCE.

• If the cascade event criteria is not met, then cascade analysis will be continued through the IROL
   Analysis Tool and manually by SOE and RC as needed.

• Not bound by the 30 minute or Tv resolution requirement of an IROL but is to be mitigated without
   intentional delay.


                                                                                             85
 Local Transmission Emergency (LTE)
 Local Transmission Emergency

A Local Transmission Emergency (LTE)…

• Should be declared when conditions do not meet PCE criteria and only exceed SOLs, in
 which the MISO RC expects NOT to be able to mitigate using normal procedures in a
 timely fashion in coordination with the TOP.
• Can be used to increase situational awareness for neighboring areas.
• Is used to be able to apply emergency mitigation tools.
